title: UDLM Composition Record — a composition nobody is offering (yet)
description: A composition that EXISTS but that nobody is standing behind: ingested from a LikeC4 diagram, converted from CALM, or authored by a consumer for themselves. It carries the same composition shape a class does (composition.schema.json — one shape, so promotion is not a translation) and deliberately none of the class machinery. WHY THIS KIND EXISTS: ordering something must never mint an entry in the shared vocabulary. If a composition were always a class, importing a diagram would add to the portable, curated, governed type registry, and so would a consumer saving a favourite — a document someone wrote is not a claim about shared vocabulary. WHAT SEPARATES IT FROM A CLASS IS GOVERNANCE, NOT STRUCTURE: the test is one question — is someone standing behind this as an offer, or did someone write it down? An offer carries `supports` (the ranges a consumer picks from) and is checked against its parent; this kind carries neither, by construction, and `additionalProperties: false` is what makes 'not an offer' structural rather than a convention. It may be realized by its author; it may never be presented to anyone else (ING-016). A composition reaches CANONICAL by being PROMOTED into a class through the governed process (ING-017), and it survives that promotion as the provenance the class points back to (ING-018) — so re-ingesting the same source next quarter diffs against it instead of looking like a brand-new composition. Ingestion of a composition is the ingestion contract one level up: the same act as bringing a brownfield entity into governance, which is why these rules are ING and not a new family (T7).

record_type.description: Dispatch discriminator (data-model-core §2). The kind is `composition` — what the thing IS. Where it sits in the governed process is `state`, which is a different question: a lifecycle state is not a definition of what something is.

uuid.description: RFC 9562 v4, minted once at creation and immutable — including across promotion. The class minted from this record is a NEW artifact with its own identity; this uuid is what the class points back to.

conforms_to.description: The UDLM spec version this record conforms to (`udlm/0.1`).

handle.description: Advisory human identity. Deliberately NOT required to be unique across the estate the way a class name is: a class name enters the shared vocabulary and is expensive to get wrong, while two teams may each have written down their own `three-tier-app` and neither is making a claim about anyone else's.

tenant_uuid.description: The tenant this composition belongs to — REQUIRED, and it is the field that makes 'not offered to others' meaningful. A class has no tenant because it is portable vocabulary; a composition record is a document owned by somebody, and that ownership is the boundary. Promotion is precisely the act of a composition leaving one tenant's ownership and becoming shared vocabulary.

state.description: Where this composition sits in the governed promotion process — the SAME ladder decision records use, deliberately not a second one (DR-UDLM-002 §6: the advancement ladder is ours and must not be re-imported). PROPOSED = authored or ingested, exactly as a freshly written ADR is Proposed. UNDER_REVIEW = nominated as a class; nomination is a distinct, recordable act, which is what makes the process auditable rather than a decision that happened once and left no trace. CANONICAL = accepted, and a class exists (`promoted_to`). DEPRECATED = superseded or withdrawn.

provenance.description: Where this composition came from, and how much of it a reader should trust. 'Where did this come from, and is it authoritative?' is a first-class question for this kind precisely because it arrives six different ways (#405).

arrival.description: How it got here. LikeC4 and CALM are mapped in docs/research/architecture-as-code-ingestion.md (nodes → entities, relationships → relationships, controls → policy seed data). Extensible: a source nobody has met yet is a new arrival path, not a defect.

origin.description: Whether a human wrote this composition or it was synthesized from an external artifact — the SAME vocabulary the realized-entity states carry, and for the same reason: inferred content is never silently presented as human-declared. An ingested diagram is `discovered-derived` however clean the mapping was.

source_ref.description: The external artifact this came from — a repository path, a document URL, an export identifier. What a re-ingest next quarter matches against to find this record rather than creating a second one.

author.description: Who wrote or ingested this. Distinct from the owner a promoted class acquires: authorship is a fact about the past, ownership is a standing commitment.

constituents.description: The parts and how they wire — THE SAME SHAPE a class composes with. One shape is the point: promotion must not be a translation, because a translation is where meaning is quietly lost and where two semantic checkers start to disagree.

composition_visibility.description: How constituents surface as first-class entities once realized. Optional here, unlike on a class: whoever ingested a diagram may simply not have expressed it, and inventing an answer would present a guess as a declaration.

refines.description: The composition this one refines — a reference to another composition record. This is where the pattern → template chain lives: one drawing yields many cuts, so the chain is REFERENCES between records rather than states of one record, because states are 1:1 and that cardinality is not. Absent means this is the top of its chain. Never a copy of what it refines: the chain is walked, not flattened (DRV-001).

promoted_to.description: The class minted from this composition — present exactly when `state` is CANONICAL (ING-017). The pointer is what makes promotion a round trip rather than a one-way copy: the class names the composition it came from, and the composition names the class it became.

then.description: CANONICAL means a class exists. A composition claiming acceptance without naming what it became records an outcome nobody can verify.

else.description: And the converse: naming a class you were promoted into, while not being CANONICAL, is the same claim made twice as loudly and once falsely.

metadata.description: Imported from the storefront architecture diagram; nobody is offering this.
